conflicts.fact: Electron configuration notation taught and used for the same elements
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 teaches s/p notation (Na: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s¹) and Bohr shell diagrams. Lesson 5 says to use 'the notation from Lesson 3 (e.g., 2,8,1 for Na)', which is shell notation, not the s/p notation Lesson 3 taught.

conflicts.fact: Group numbering system (Roman numerals vs Arabic 1/2/17/18)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 uses Groups I, VII, VIII/0 (8 groups across a 4x8 grid) while Lessons 4-5 and 6 use Groups 1, 2, 16, 17, 18 without reconciling the systems. Lesson 3 states group number equals outer electrons (Group VII = 7), but Lesson 4 uses Group 17 for halogens.

conflicts.fact: Which elements are in Group I / alkali metals in the 20-element set
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 lines up Group I elements as H, Li, Na, K, treating H as Group I. Lesson 4 lists Group 1 alkali metals as Li, Na, K only, excluding hydrogen.

conflicts.fact: Lessons in which model is revised / where electron arrangement is first explained
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says Model Version 1 will be revised at the end of Lessons 5, 10, 15, 20 and 30, but the sub-strand has only 10 lessons and the model is revised every lesson (Lessons 2, 3, 4, 5, ...).

conflicts.fact: Unbalanced vs balanced equation for sodium and water
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 Observe says the teacher writes the unbalanced symbol equation as '2Na + 2H2O → 2NaOH + H2', which is already balanced, while the teacher's actions say the unbalanced equation is 'Na + H2O → NaOH + H2'.

conflicts.fact: Kenyan location of chlorine water treatment and the calcium/sodium contexts
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 overview links chlorine to Mombasa water treatment, while its Predict phase and Lessons 1, 3, 7 and 10 use the Gigiri plant in Nairobi. Lesson 5 uses both Gigiri and Mombasa.

conflicts.fact: Number of cards in the Lesson 1 model sketch and what students sketched
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 model building has students draw a blank-grid sketch with a Model Panel of the inside of two elements. Lesson 2 refers to this as a diagram showing how they would arrange a subset of 10 cards, and Lesson 1's card sort uses all 20.

conflicts.fact: Card used to teach Group structure / which cards are paired
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 compares Li/Na, F/Cl and He/Ne as example pairs, while Lesson 3 uses Na/K and Ne/Ar. Lesson 1 numbers cards by Z (Card 3 = Li, Card 11 = Na, 17 = Cl, 20 = Ca) but Lesson 1's own card backs are numbered 1-20 arbitrarily, so the teasers fit only if the order is by atomic number.
